correctness.rationale: On the explicit positive-inhibition interior B_H>0 with s>0, s<r<s+1 and 0<tildeX<1/(s+1), the normalized Jacobian J(1,1) has Tr=r[(p-p_c)-Bq/(1+B)] and det=r[1/X1-p+Bq/(1+B)]. At B_H=q_c/(q-q_c), det=r(1/X1-p_c)=rs*tildeX/X1-1; det>0 iff tildeX>1/(s+1+sr). This also gives p_c<1/X1, so source Prop.3.1 Hopf branches cover exactly p>p_c, q>q_c with B=B_H. The additional high-p q>q1 condition at B_H is q-q1=q(1-p_c X1)/(q_c X1)>0, the same determinant inequality. With K adjusted by the equilibrium relation, d_B Re(lambda)|BH=-r*q/(2(1+B_H)^2)=-r(q-q_c)^2/(2q)<0. The exact reparametrization gives omega_H²=D; source focus frequency includes the positive factor 1+B_H. All 12 fresh SymPy checks passed, including independently differentiated Jacobian and 2011 general-incidence normalization; rational sample (s,r,T,p,q)=(1,3/2,1/3,3,2) gives B_H=1/5, omega²=1/2, crossing=-25/24. The assertion is correct as a local spectral Hopf crossing criterion, not a theorem of nondegenerate nonlinear Hopf cycles, first Lyapunov coefficient, or all B=0 boundary configurations. Malformed source LaTeX control characters were resolved through the clean primary equations, not ignored.

evidence: Hu et al. (2011) pp.95,102 in the same SIRS framework with arbitrary incidence f(I) give equilibrium f(I_e)[N0-I_e-R_e]=(d+mu)I_e, R_e=mu I_e/(d+v), and omega_c²=mu f(I_e)-(d+v)² at Hopf.
Setting tildeX=I_e/N0, s=mu/(d+v), r=(d+mu)/(d+v), X1=1-(1+s)tildeX gives omega_c²/(d+v)² = r s tildeX/X1-1, exactly the candidate frequency formula for a more general incidence function.
Yu et al. (2026) Proposition 3.1 and Eq.(21) already cover the full positive-inhibition Hopf locus for this p/q incidence.

originality.rationale: The claimed one-line locus, crossing and D identity are algebraic consequences of Yu–Tang–Zeng (2026) equations (18),(21),(30)–(34). More importantly, Hu–Bi–Ma–Ruan (2011) already give a general-incidence endemic Hopf frequency omega_c²=mu*f(I_e)-(d+v)²; combined with its endemic-equilibrium equation, this yields the identical normalized frequency rs*tildeX/X1-1 for any incidence function. The present p/q model is a special case. Neither title uniqueness nor failure to find a matching table establishes mathematical novelty.
residual_risks: The standard phrase ordinary/nondegenerate Hopf would require a nonzero first Lyapunov coefficient; the exact algebra proves the simple imaginary crossing locus only. Codimension-5 generalized Hopf points in the source lie on the same linear Hopf locus. The result explicitly disclaims Lyapunov-coefficient classification; interpret Hopf criterion in that restricted spectral sense.
The equilibrium-preserving B-variation varies K simultaneously. The incidence-exponent independence holds at fixed s,r,tildeX, not freely varied dimensional parameters.

value.rationale: The onset frequency is a natural epidemiological invariant and a clearer parametrization could help readers. But the proposed contribution is entirely mechanical elimination, time-scale substitution and rephrasing of the same published Hopf criterion, plus a special case of the broader 2011 general-incidence frequency law. It introduces no new boundary, independent exact invariant, structural classification or non-implied mathematical phenomenon. Hence this submission has no distinct incremental mathematical value as a scientific finding, despite the relevance of the subject.
residual_risks: A clear pedagogic interpretation can have expository utility, but it is not a new mathematical result under the requested V bar.
